comments.message:
Hi,

I’m using the Styles & Variables Organizer plugin to replace remote variables with local ones. It works great for visible layers, but it currently skips any layers that are hidden.

It would be really helpful if the plugin could also detect and process variables used on hidden layers. Many of us keep components or elements hidden (like alternate states or unused variants) that still rely on variables, and having to manually reveal them all before running the plugin is a pain.

Adding support for hidden layers would make variable migration much smoother and more complete.

Thanks for considering this!

comments.message:
Hi everyone! Thanks for all the suggestions and feedback. I have shipped the following updates for the plugin:


* Scan selected elements only, allowing more control over the elements to organize
* Improved scanning speed and error handling
* Improved display of variable modes

Figma has updated its API for variable mode detection, so the plugin will not filter elements by modes now. It is recommended to select elements of the same mode and scan at a time.

Although I have done extensive testing on my end, it is hard to account for all possible scenarios in a Figma file, so please help give the new version a try and lemme know what you think or report any issues that you find. Thank you very much!

comments.message:
Nice plugin.. one issue that I had with it. When scanning for unlinked variables, you have a useful feature to merge several ones of the same value. However the logic of this is a bit frustrating.

If I have the variable rem/1 = 16 and I have that and some unlinked 16 values.. the merge works nicely.

However.. if I have another variable that happens to have the same value in the current mode, there is no way to merge the unlinked variables without also merging both the linked variable types together.

The UI already has 2 of the merge icons, so I'd love if the first click would merge the unlinked variables into the selected variable, then once there were only linked variables, you could merge like now.

Even better would be checkboxes to select which to merge where, or a dropdown to assign these to a variable.

Thanks
